timeline.title: Evolutionary Milestones of Global Governance
timeline.description: Key historical and recent milestones shaping the United Nations, G20, and BRICS groupings.

cards.details: The UN Charter entered into force after ratification by the five permanent members of the Security Council and a majority of other signatories. India was among the founding members.
Founded in the wake of the Asian financial crisis as a forum for Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors to discuss global economic and financial issues.
The leaders of Brazil, Russia, India, and China met in Yekaterinburg, Russia, establishing the BRIC group. South Africa was formally invited to join in December 2010, making it BRICS.
Under India's presidency, the G20 adopted the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration by consensus and formally admitted the African Union as a permanent member.
The 16th BRICS Summit was held in Kazan, Russia, marking the first summit after the official expansion of the group to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the UAE.

items.question: Who is the current Secretary-General of the United Nations, and what is his home country?
items.answer: António Guterres, former Prime Minister of Portugal. He assumed office on January 1, 2017, and is currently serving his second term.

items.question: Which African organization became a permanent member of the G20 during the 18th Summit in New Delhi?
items.answer: The African Union (AU), consisting of 55 member states, was admitted as a permanent member under India's G20 Presidency.

items.question: Name the four cities in Uttar Pradesh that hosted G20 meetings during India's presidency.
items.answer: Varanasi, Lucknow, Agra, and Greater Noida.

items.question: Which country declined the invitation to join BRICS in late 2023, despite being approved for membership?
items.answer: Argentina, under the leadership of President Javier Milei, formally declined the invitation to join the bloc.

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: The G20 Headquarters Fallacy: Candidates often get confused and look for a permanent headquarters or secretariat for G20. Remember: G20 does NOT have a permanent secretariat or headquarters. It operates on a rotating presidency supported by the Troika.

ICJ vs. ICC Jurisdiction and Status: Do not confuse the International Court of Justice (ICJ) with the International Criminal Court (ICC). ICJ is a principal organ of the UN and settles disputes between states. ICC is an independent treaty-based body (Rome Statute) that prosecutes individuals; India is NOT a member of the ICC.

BRICS Expansion Membership Status: Questions may list Saudi Arabia as a fully integrated member. While Saudi Arabia was invited and participates, as of mid-2024, it has not officially completed the formal integration process. Argentina formally rejected the invitation. Only Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and UAE officially joined on Jan 1, 2024.

deepDive.title: International Organizations: UN, G20, and BRICS Core Study Notes
deepDive.description: This comprehensive study guide covers the structural frameworks, recent summits, and geopolitical significance of the United Nations (UN), G20, and BRICS. Designed specifically for the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC exams, it highlights India's leadership roles, key administrative appointments, and specific events hosted in Uttar Pradesh.

sections.title: United Nations (UN): Organs, Key Appointments & India
sections.content:
The United Nations remains the cornerstone of multilateralism. Understanding its principal organs and India's active diplomatic engagements is vital for state civil services.

  • Principal Organs and Headquarters: The UN has six principal organs: General Assembly (UNGA), Security Council (UNSC), Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), Trusteeship Council, International Court of Justice (ICJ - located in The Hague, Netherlands), and the Secretariat. All except the ICJ are headquartered in New York.
  • UN Security Council (UNSC) Structure: Consists of 15 members: 5 permanent members (P5: US, UK, France, Russia, China) with veto power, and 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms by the UNGA. India has served as a non-permanent member eight times, most recently in 2021-2022.
  • India's Permanent Representative to the UN: Senior diplomat Parvathaneni Harish was appointed as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York in August 2024, succeeding Ruchira Kamboj.
  • UN General Assembly (UNGA) 79th Session: The 79th session of the UNGA opened in September 2024. Philemon Yang of Cameroon was elected as the President of the 79th session. The theme focused on unity in diversity for the advancement of peace, sustainable development, and human dignity.

sections.title: G20: India's Presidency and Uttar Pradesh Connect
sections.content:
India's G20 Presidency from December 1, 2022, to November 30, 2023, was a landmark event. It showcased India's cultural heritage and leadership in the Global South, with significant events hosted in Uttar Pradesh.

  • Theme and Logo: The theme of India's G20 Presidency was 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' or 'One Earth · One Family · One Future', drawn from the ancient Sanskrit text of the Maha Upanishad. The logo featured a blooming lotus with the Earth.
  • Historic Inclusion of the African Union: Under India's initiative, the African Union (AU) was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 during the New Delhi Summit, making the group more representative of the Global South.
  • G20 Meetings in Uttar Pradesh: Uttar Pradesh hosted 11 G20 meetings across four cities: Varanasi, Lucknow, Agra, and Greater Noida. Key meetings included the G20 Development Ministers' Meeting in Varanasi (chaired by EAM S. Jaishankar) and the Digital Economy Working Group Meeting in Lucknow.
  • G20 Troika: The G20 Troika consists of the previous, current, and incoming presidencies. During India's presidency, the Troika comprised Indonesia, India, and Brazil. Currently (2024), it comprises India, Brazil, and South Africa.

sections.title: BRICS: Expansion and Geopolitical Realignment
sections.content:
BRICS has evolved from an investment acronym into a powerful geopolitical bloc representing major emerging economies, challenging traditional Western-dominated financial systems.

  • The 2024 Expansion: Effective January 1, 2024, BRICS officially welcomed four new members: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Saudi Arabia was invited and participates in activities but has not finalized formal integration. Argentina declined the invitation.
  • 16th BRICS Summit (Kazan, Russia): Held in October 2024 under the theme 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security'. It was the first summit attended by the newly expanded membership. The 'Kazan Declaration' was adopted.
  • New Development Bank (NDB): Established during the 6th BRICS Summit in Fortaleza (2014) with an initial authorized capital of $100 billion. Headquartered in Shanghai, China. Dilma Rousseff (former President of Brazil) is the current President of NDB.
  • Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA): A framework established by BRICS in 2015 to provide protection against global liquidity pressures. It acts as a financial safety net for member countries during balance of payment crises.

sections.title: Comparative Analysis of Global Groupings
sections.content:
A quick comparative reference of the major international organizations frequently asked in UPPSC and AHC RO/ARO exams.

  • Structural Differences: While the UN is a treaty-based international organization with a permanent charter and legal personality, G20 and BRICS are informal consensus-based groupings without permanent secretariats.
